title: run.json
description: R-D4: the record of one run (identity, code, problem, host, lineage, status). Written at start and updated only in its `status` block. `key` is sha256 hex of the RFC 8785 canonical form of {"problem": run.problem, "params": <values of params.json>}; it is required unless the record is `provenance: "imported"` (R-D11: an import has a key only when the full parameter set was recovered). The key is verified by run-check, not by this schema. Choices where the plan is silent: objects are open (unknown fields are kept, TR-D13); terminal states (done, failed, cancelled) require `ended_at` and `exit`; the exit-code bands are enforced here.

convention.description: The version of the run convention this record follows.

id.description: UUID minted at start; not a hash (R-D4.1).

name.description: Human alias, free text, not unique.

provenance.description: Absent means native. `imported` marks a record built by an importer from an old run folder (R-D11).

diff_sha256.description: Hash of the diff when dirty; the diff itself is a blob.

lock_sha256.description: Hash of the environment lock file (Manifest.toml).

problem.description: R-D2.4: the named, versioned generator of the initial state and its own parameters. This whole object is part of the key.

inputs.description: Input files recorded by content hash (R-D4.2).

parent.description: The run this one resumed from or forked from. A restart asserts what it resumed from (R-D4.2).

sweep.description: The `id` of the sweep.json this run belongs to (R-D10).

status.description: The only block that changes after start (R-D4.2).

state.description: R-D4.4. `orphaned` is derived by a tool and never written.

exit.description: R-D4.5. Bands: 0 ok; 100-199 stopped by environment; 200-299 invalid input; 300-399 numerical failure; 400-499 code-specific. Nothing else is a valid exit code.

invalidates_reuse.description: On a failure: the run must not be treated as the answer for its key.
